title: HC phasing and price elasticity tool — June 2025
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This working sheet is intended to be a compact, scenario-driven tool for: 1) phasing headcount (HC) hires across engineering, product and GTM for the next 12–18 months, 2) estimating the near-term P&L impact (monthly cadence) of those hires, and 3) running instant pricing sensitivity checks to compute break-even price changes vs. margin and retention assumptions.

High-level assumptions (visible inputs):
- Time window: Jul 2025 — Dec 2026 (18 months), monthly buckets.
- Currency: USD.
- Hiring ramp: hires are assumed to join at the start of the month; ramp-to-productivity = 3 months for ICs, 2 months for ops/CS, 6 months for senior ICs/EMs.
- Fully loaded cost per hire (avg): IC engineer = 220k/year, senior engineer = 330k/year, product manager = 260k/year, SRE/infra = 240k/year, sales AE = 200k/year, CSM = 150k/year. Benefits/headcount tax = included in fully loaded.
- Infra/cloud base runrate (non-hire): 1.8M/year; per-100k inference requests incremental cloud = 20k/month (workload dependent).
- Existing ARR (starting point): $45M (monthly recognized: $3.75M).
- Gross margin baseline (current): 68% (after direct cloud & infra).
- Customer elasticity sensitivity: modeled as four segments: low-elasticity (L: 0–2% churn per +5% price), medium (M: 2–6%), high (H: 6–12%), strategic accounts (S: assumed price-insensitive).

Scenario definitions (quick):
- Base: hiring plan aligned to Q3 roadmap (~+24 HC net over 12 months), conservative retention, no price change.
- Efficiency-first: hiring paused for non-critical roles; prioritize cost controls (defer 60% of hires), more aggressive infra optimizations, consider +5% price if needed.
- Growth-aggressive: accelerate HC by +40% vs Base, hire for Dedicated & Private sales push; accept higher short-term margin pressure.
- Downside / Defend-cash: hiring freeze, 10–15% variable cost cut, test price increases early to shore up cash.

Sheet excerpt: headcount phasing (sample months shown) — monthly hire counts by bucket:
Month, eng_ic_new, eng_sr_new, product_new, infra_new, sales_new, csm_new
2025-07, 3, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1
2025-08, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0
2025-09, 2, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1
2025-10, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0
2025-11, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1
2025-12, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0
(…continues through 2026-12)

Monthly cost derivation (formula notes):
- Monthly cost per hire = fully_loaded_annual / 12.
- Ramp discount factor: 0% productivity in month 0, 50% month1, 75% month2, 100% month3 (adjustable by role). This affects revenue contribution attribution and hiring ROI months.
- Headcount Opex impact flows into R&D (eng/product), S&M (sales/CS), and G&A (small misc hires).

Sample 3-scenario 6-month P&L delta table (Jul-Dec 2025):
Row labels: ARR start, incremental ARR from hires (modeled conservatively), direct cloud incremental, HC cost incremental, gross margin %, net burn change
Base: ARR start 3.75M/mo; incremental ARR 0.08M -> cloud +0.02M -> HC +0.45M -> gross margin ~66% -> net burn +0.39M/mo (from hires)
Efficiency-first: incremental ARR 0.05M -> cloud +0.01M -> HC +0.18M -> gross margin ~67.5% -> net burn +0.12M/mo
Growth-aggressive: incremental ARR 0.15M -> cloud +0.05M -> HC +0.63M -> gross margin ~63% -> net burn +0.53M/mo

Pricing sensitivity module (how to use) — inputs that can be toggled:
- Price delta (%) applied to hosted API unit prices (tokens / embeddings / features).
- Elasticity bucket mapping: percent of ARR in L/M/H/S segments (default: L 30%, M 40%, H 25%, S 5%).
- Churn response function: for +5% price, L-> +1% churn, M-> +4%, H-> +9%, S-> +0%. We scale linearly for other price deltas.
- Upsell / net expansion factor: price increase may increase ARPA on remaining accounts by 50% of price delta (offset).

Example outputs for a +5% price increase (applied immediately):
- Gross revenue effect (gross): +5% applied to 100% of ARR = +3.75M * 0.05 = +0.1875M/mo (pure math)
- Retention hit (ARR lost): L: 30%*3.75M * 1% = 0.01125M; M: 40% * 3.75M * 4% = 0.06M; H: 25% * 3.75M * 9% = 0.084375M; S: 5% * 3.75M * 0% = 0.0M; total lost ARR = 0.155625M/mo
- Net revenue delta = +0.1875M - 0.155625M = +0.031875M/mo (~+32k/mo)
- Margin/COGS effect: assume price increase has near-zero incremental COGS, so gross margin improves slightly on retained ARR; but if lost ARR was higher-margin accounts, margin could fall — see sensitivity toggle.
- Break-even price increase that nets zero revenue uplift (ignoring expansion): solve for price_delta where price_delta * ARR = churn_loss(price_delta). With default elasticities, break-even near +4.4% in this example.

Sensitivity sweep recommendations (quick):
- If >40% of ARR maps to H bucket, avoid >3% across-the-board price changes; prefer segmented/exempted pricing for S/strategic accounts.
- Prefer usage-based increases on new customers only; grandfather existing customers for 6–12 months where possible.
- Consider revenue-based thresholds: increases that produce <50k/mo uplift are not worth the churn/CS effort unless margin is critical.

Cash runway & headcount tradeoff dashboard (instructions):
- Input cash balance, monthly non-HC cash burn, and planned hire schedule. The sheet computes runway in months under each scenario.
- Key trigger rules (examples):
  - If runway < 9 months, freeze non-essential hires and reclassify 30% planned hires to delayed buckets.
  - If net burn from hiring increases >25% vs prior quarter, require exec sign-off and alternative cost offsets in infra or contractor reduction.

Open questions / manual checks (notes to reviewers):
- We need role-level hire-level true-up: some hiring will be contractors to reduce ramp and cost; model currently treats contractor FTE as 60% cost of full hire but immediate productivity — need contractor pipeline input from People Ops.
- Elasticity buckets are coarse; product/packaging team should provide seat/license vs usage revenue splits to refine model.
- Should we model multi-year retention effects of price changes? Current model is 1-month immediate churn and does not model longer tail attrition.

Action items / next steps:
- Maya to add People Ops hiring queue (by role + start month) — due 2025-07-08.
- Leo to map current ARR into elasticity buckets using last 12 months revenue by account — due 2025-06-20.
- Finance to run sensitivity sweep script (attached link) and produce three charts: runway vs hires, net revenue delta vs price, and margin impact heatmap — due 2025-07-10.
- Ops to provide infra optimization levers (expected $/month at 3 levels) for the Efficiency-first scenario.

Quick appendix (scratch calculations):
- Monthly cost for 1 eng IC = 220k/12 = ~18.3k/mo. For 10 ICs added = ~183k/mo incremental HC runrate (steady state).
- If we defer 60% of planned hires (from Base) for 6 months, recurring monthly HC savings = ~110–140k/mo depending on role mix.
- A targeted +5% price in hosted API that affects only usage-based customers (60% of ARR) produces ~0.1875M*0.6 = ~112.5k/mo gross uplift before churn, with churn expected mostly from usage-sensitive customers.

Notes to CFO / Finance leadership (one-liner):
This is a compact scenario tool — not a replacement for the full FY26 plan. Use it to evaluate tradeoffs quickly prior to board conversations; major hires and a company-wide price change both materially affect runway, but targeted, segmented price moves + infra optimizations deliver better margin leverage than across-the-board increases.
